added_models.model: Human 19-28z CAR T cells in SCID-beige mice bearing intraperitoneal Raji tumours (CRS model)

safety.population: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (unselected; CD19 assumed)
safety.confidence_note: Opening entry at first use (epub 28 May 2018).
safety.note: Built after clinical CAR T CRS was known, using MSKCC's 19-28z CAR (not a member product).
safety.quote: Here we report a murine model of CRS that develops within 2-3 d of CAR T cell infusion and that is potentially lethal and responsive to IL-6 receptor blockade.
safety.model: Human 19-28z CAR T cells in SCID-beige mice bearing intraperitoneal Raji tumours (CRS model)

safety.magnitude_basis: serum cytokine profile vs clinical CRS reports and IL-6R-blockade response
safety.population: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (unselected; CD19 assumed)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read for the ALL tile (PMC6410714); clinical cytokine comparators are mainly CD19 CAR T in ALL, so imported. Citation markers dropped from quote.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: clinical CRS preceded the model. 19-28z is not axi-cel/liso-cel/relma-cel, so product_in_model false. No neurotoxicity in mice, hence partial.
safety.note: Reproduced clinical CRS cytokines and IL-6R-blockade rescue, but no neurotoxicity, which LBCL patients on axi-cel had.
safety.quote: Remarkably, the serum cytokine profile elicited in these mice was highly similar to that reported in clinical studies
safety.model: Human 19-28z CAR T cells in SCID-beige mice bearing intraperitoneal Raji tumours (CRS model)

added_models.model: CD19 CAR T cells in HSPC-humanized NSG-SGM3 mice with high leukaemia burden (CRS/neurotoxicity model)

safety.population: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (unselected; CD19 assumed)
safety.confidence_note: Opening entry at first use (epub 28 May 2018).
safety.note: Humanized-mouse model built after clinical CRS and neurotoxicity were known, to reproduce both.
safety.quote: Herein, we describe a mouse model recapitulating key features of CRS and neurotoxicity.
safety.model: CD19 CAR T cells in HSPC-humanized NSG-SGM3 mice with high leukaemia burden (CRS/neurotoxicity model)

safety.magnitude_basis: fever, IL-6 rise and delayed lethal neurotoxicity vs clinical CAR T toxicity
safety.population: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (unselected; CD19 assumed)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only (paywalled); model tumour is ALL, clinical comparators are CAR T toxicity generally, so imported.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction; research CD19 CAR, not a member product, so product_in_model false. CD44v6-CAR arms are a sibling target and not the basis of the call.
safety.note: Reproduced burden-dependent CRS with IL-6 and delayed neurotoxicity, as seen with CD19 CAR T in patients.
safety.quote: In humanized mice with high leukemia burden, CAR T cell-mediated clearance of cancer triggered high fever and elevated IL-6 levels, which are hallmarks of CRS.
safety.model: CD19 CAR T cells in HSPC-humanized NSG-SGM3 mice with high leukaemia burden (CRS/neurotoxicity model)

added_models.model: Defined-composition CD4+/CD8+ CD19-41BB CAR T cells (liso-cel) in immunodeficient mice engrafted with CD19+ tumour

efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (unselected; CD19 assumed)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read; opening entry at first use (epub 15 Sep 2015). Riddell-lab research product that became JCAR017.
efficacy.note: Defined CD4:CD8 CD19 CAR T cells gave synergistic antitumour activity in NSG lymphoma xenografts, liso-cel's preclinical basis.
efficacy.quote: Combining the most potent CD4(+) and CD8(+) CAR-expressing subsets, resulted in synergistic antitumor effects in vivo.
efficacy.model: Defined-composition CD4+/CD8+ CD19-41BB CAR T cells (liso-cel) in immunodeficient mice engrafted with CD19+ tumour

efficacy.magnitude_basis: objective response rate vs xenograft tumour regression
efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (unselected; CD19 assumed)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract read. NCT02631044 has no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov (checked 2026-11-07). Model side from the CBER SBRA (Feb 2021): 'Dose-dependent anti-tumor activity and improved animal survival were demonstrated in immunocompromised rodent models engrafted with CD19-expressing tumor cells following administration of BREYANZI.'
efficacy.judgement: Paired: the CBER SBRA records liso-cel's own xenograft efficacy; TRANSCEND NHL 001 ORR (a primary endpoint) met. The model's dose-dependence did not carry over (no dose-response across 50-150x10^6), not scored here since the model stated no human dose.
efficacy.note: Liso-cel, effective in CD19+ xenografts, gave a 73% objective response in relapsed/refractory LBCL in TRANSCEND NHL 001.
efficacy.quote: Of 256 patients included in the efficacy-evaluable set, an objective response was achieved by 186 (73%, 95% CI 66·8-78·0) patients and a complete response by 136 (53%, 46·8-59·4).
efficacy.model: Defined-composition CD4+/CD8+ CD19-41BB CAR T cells (liso-cel) in immunodeficient mice engrafted with CD19+ tumour

added_models.model: Single-cell polyfunctionality (PSI) of each patient's preinfusion CD19 CAR T product, stimulated ex vivo with CD19+ targets

efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (unselected; CD19 assumed)
efficacy.confidence_note: Opening entry at first use (epub 12 Jun 2018); abstract read.
efficacy.note: Ex-vivo single-cell cytokine profiling of each patient's preinfusion FMC63-28Z (axi-cel construct) product, to predict who responds.
efficacy.quote: A single-cell analysis of the preinfusion CD19 CAR product from patients with NHL demonstrated that CAR products contain polyfunctional T-cell subsets capable of deploying multiple immune programs represented by cytokines and chemokines
efficacy.model: Single-cell polyfunctionality (PSI) of each patient's preinfusion CD19 CAR T product, stimulated ex vivo with CD19+ targets

efficacy.magnitude_basis: association of PSI with objective response
efficacy.population: Relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma (unselected; CD19 assumed)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only. Cohort is mixed NHL from NCT00924326 (NCI FMC63-28Z, the academic axi-cel product, as the draft accepts); LBCL share not verified. Exploratory, no prospective validation found.
efficacy.judgement: Counted as an ex-vivo patient-level model (each patient's product stimulated against CD19 targets), not mere product phenotyping. Retrodiction: assayed on banked products after responses were known, though the index was prespecified.
efficacy.note: Preinfusion product polyfunctionality was associated with clinical response in NHL patients; exploratory and after the fact.
efficacy.quote: A prespecified T-cell polyfunctionality strength index (PSI) applied to preinfusion CAR product was significantly associated with clinical response
efficacy.model: Single-cell polyfunctionality (PSI) of each patient's preinfusion CD19 CAR T product, stimulated ex vivo with CD19+ targets

considered_not_added: Rhesus macaque CAR T CRS/neurotoxicity model (Taraseviciute 2018): CD20 CAR, a sibling target outside the class

Kochenderfer 2010 Blood case report (B-cell aplasia, FMC63-28Z, follicular lymphoma): an earlier patient comparison on the draft's existing syngeneic-mcd19-car-mouse track (engagement/safety), not a new system
Axi-cel product attributes (CCR7+CD45RA+ T cells, Locke 2020 Blood Adv) and tumour burden/IL-6 correlates: product phenotyping and patient covariates, not a model system run on the patient's cells
Relma-cel (JW Therapeutics): licensed JCAR017 platform; no separately published preclinical model compared with patients found
In-silico cellular-kinetic / QSP models of axi-cel (e.g. ZUMA-1 kinetics fits): fitted to clinical data, none used to choose a dose prospectively found
Liso-cel xenograft dose-dependence: model stated no human dose, exposure or margin, so no dose cell added
Kite axi-cel nonclinical package: the murine surrogate syngeneic model the draft already tracks
